This article is divided into two parts: equality before the law, which means all are to be treated equally in the eyes of the law, and equal protection of the laws, which means the same law will be applied to all the people equally across the country. The doctrine of anti-arbitrariness is also included in Article 14, which ensures equality of treatment and prevents the arbitrary actions of the State. Natural justice is also an integral part of Article 14. The classification test is used to determine whether differential classification is founded on intelligible differentia and has a rational nexus with the objective sought to be achieved by the classification. The Supreme Court has expanded the scope of Article 14 to include gender equality and the recognition of persons who fall outside the male/Female gender binary.

dataset_citation_key: Article 21 in Constitution of India
canonical_text: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
nyayarag_dataset_text_raw: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the fundamental right to protection of life and personal liberty. It ensures that no person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. This right includes the right to live with dignity, the right to livelihood, and the right to a healthy environment. It also protects personal liberty, which includes the freedom to move freely, choose one's place of residence, and engage in any lawful occupation or profession. Reasonable restrictions can be imposed on these rights in the interests of public order, national security, public health, or morality. The interpretation and scope of Article 21 have expanded through various landmark judgments, including the recognition of the right to privacy, the right to die with dignity, and protection against torture, custodial violence, and the right to a clean and healthy environment.

dataset_citation_key: Article 31 in Constitution of India
canonical_text: [Omitted] Compulsory acquisition of property. Article 31 was deleted from Part III of the Constitution by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978; a modified property-right provision was reinserted as Article 300A outside the fundamental-rights chapter.
nyayarag_dataset_text_raw: Article 31 of the Indian Constitution, which dealt with the right to property, was repealed and replaced by Article 300A through the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act in 1978. Article 300A now states that no person shall be deprived of his or her property except by the authority of law. It ensures that if the state acquires private property for public purposes, it must do so in accordance with the law and provide fair compensation to the affected individuals. This provision protects individuals against arbitrary deprivation of their property by the state. However, it is no longer a fundamental right and is instead a legal right under the Constitution.

dataset_citation_key: Article 133 in Constitution of India
canonical_text: An appeal shall lie to the Supreme Court from any judgment, decree or final order in a civil proceeding of a High Court if the High Court certifies that the case involves a substantial question of law of general importance and that the question needs to be decided by the Supreme Court.
nyayarag_dataset_text_raw: Article 133 of the Indian Constitution outlines the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in civil matters arising from High Courts. An appeal can be made to the Supreme Court from any final civil order, judgment, or decree of a High Court if the High Court certifies that the case involves a substantial question of law of general importance that needs to be decided by the Supreme Court. The appealing party may also raise a substantial question of law related to the Constitution's interpretation. However, no appeal can be made to the Supreme Court from the judgment, decree, or final order of a single High Court judge unless Parliament provides otherwise by law. This amendment was made to streamline the process for hearing civil appeals in the Supreme Court and to require appeals to raise a substantial question of law to be considered.

canonical_text: No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest, nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by, a legal practitioner of his choice.
